ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.claim: Brief reminders about creation, life’s sources, death, and resurrection expose the transience of arrogant pride and point to Judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p182/r1.anchor: In these verses, the pride and vanity of these people is condemned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r4.claim: Exegetes commonly restrict God’s easing to delivery for mother and child, which the author accepts but broadens to providential ease from womb and birth through nourishment and human activity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p184/r4.anchor: our exegetes generally say that it refers to the easing out which providence has ordained in the body of the mother and her child for delivery

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r1.claim: God eases both material and spiritual life; following the guided path avoids stumbling, but misuse of free will leads to ruin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r1.anchor: If he treads this path, he will never stumble

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r4.claim: 87:2–3 describes God perfecting creation, setting destinies, and giving guidance; 91:7–10 says the soul receives moral direction and succeeds through purification.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p185/r4.anchor: the soul and the morals ordained in it

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r3.claim: ثم السبيل يسره means God made the way easy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r3.anchor: ثم السبيل يسره: أي ثم يسر السبيل، أي سهل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، أبو صالح، السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r4.claim: They say the path is sound reflection leading to faith, eased by granting reason.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة وأبو صالح والسدي: سبيل النظر القويم المؤدي إلى الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r5.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن، عطاء، ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r5.claim: They take the path generically as guidance or error, easing each group toward its way; other verses are cited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن وعطاء وابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح عنه: السبيل العام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r6.claim: He also says the path is the way out of the womb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p409/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: يسره للخروج من بطن أمه.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.claim: The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1.anchor: بأن المراد الأعظم تزكية القابل للخشية بالتخويف بالقيامة

ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r5.claim: Making the path easy includes the stages from birth until a person's intellect and reasoning mature.
ELMALILI:80:3-42#4/r5.anchor: doğumundan akl u fikrinin tekemmülüne kadar geçirdiği merâtibe şâmildir

SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r1.claim: One parse takes the pronoun as the human and السبيل as an adverbial: God made the road of good and evil easy for him, as in 90:10.
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون الضمير للإنسان. والسبيل ظرف، أي: يسر للإنسان الطريق، أي: طريق الخير والشر

SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows السبيل as a second object, with the pronoun referring to the human: God made the path easy for him, meaning guided him to it. Al-Samīn says this needs a causative ‘give’ sense or an omitted preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r2.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " ويجوز أن ينتصب بأنه مفعول ثان ل يسره، والهاء للإنسان، أي: يسره السبيل، أي: هداه له "

SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r3.claim: Alternatively, السبيل is fronted with an implied verb in an ishtighāl construction and the pronoun refers to the path: He made the path easy for people, as in 20:50 and 76:3.
SAMIN-DURR:80:20/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " السبيل " منصوبا على الاشتغال بفعل مقدر، والضمير له، تقديره: ثم يسر السبيل يسره، أي: سهله للناس

ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r1.claim: The phrase literally means that God makes man's way easy.
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r1.anchor: Lit., "He makes easy the way for him".

ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r2.claim: It alludes to man's intellectual equipment for distinguishing good from evil and making fruitful use of opportunities in his earthly environment.
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n7/r2.anchor: enabling him to discern between good and evil and to make fruitful use of the opportunities offered to him by his earthly environment.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r1.claim: Qatāda says the facilitated path is the child's passage out of its mother's womb.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم السبيل يسره ﴾ قال خروجه من بطن أمه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r2.claim: Mujāhid interprets the path as the alternatives of wretchedness and felicity.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r2.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق قال ابن جريج عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم السبيل يسره ﴾ قال الشقاء والسعادة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the path as the path of goodness.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p348#3/r3.anchor: قال معمر وقال الحسن سبيل الخير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the path as the newborn's way out of the womb, made easy by opening the womb, extending nerves along the passage, and turning the head downward after it had been upward.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r1.anchor: كما في رواية عن ابن عباس بأن فتح فم الرحم ومدد الأعصاب في طريقه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وأبو صالح والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi explain the path as sound reflection leading to faith; God eases it by granting reason and enabling thought.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة وأبي صالح والسدي المراد بالسبيل سبيل النظر القويم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وعطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r3.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Ata, with another report from Ibn Abbas, take the path to mean both guidance and error: God enables a person to follow either good or evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن وعطاء وهو رواية عن الحبر أيضا هو سبيل الهدى والضلال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r4.claim: Facilitating both good and evil is still an evident blessing because the person is empowered for either, regardless of the moral direction chosen.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r4.anchor: والأقدار على المراد نعمة ظاهرة بقطع النظر عن خيريته وشريته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r5.claim: Another answer counts the evil path as a blessing because one could not deserve praise and reward for turning away from it if it were not accessible like the good path; this assumes that abstention without ability is not rewarded, while another view rewards and praises one who resolves not to sin even if able.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r5.anchor: لأنه لو لم يكن مسهلا كسبيل الخير لم يستحق المدح والثواب بالأعراض عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r6.claim: Some say inability to do evil is itself a blessing and cite a Persian couplet thanking God for lacking the power to harm people.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم العجز عن الشر نعمة وأنشد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r7.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative by an implied verb explained by the following verb, intensifying ease and reinforcing it in the mind through repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r7.anchor: ونصب السبيل بمضمر يفسره الظاهر وفيه مبالغة في التيسير وتمكين في النفس بسبب التكرير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r8.claim: Some find generality in the definite article: saying his path might suggest that each person has a path peculiar to him; some limit this observation to the guidance-and-error interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r8.anchor: قيل وفي تعريفه باللام دون الإضافة إشعار بعمومه فإنه لو قيل سبيله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r9.claim: On the guidance-and-error interpretation, the verse hints that worldly life is a path whose destination lies elsewhere, since the path leads to reward or punishment; al-Alusi calls this implication obscure.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r9.anchor: وعلى هذا المعنى قيل إن فيه إيماء إلى أن الدنيا طريق والمقصد غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r10.claim: The object pronoun in yassara refers to al-sabīl; the intervening material creates no ambiguity or defect in clarity.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p44#3/r10.anchor: فالضمير المنصوب في يسره للسبيل وليس في التفكيك لبس حتى يكون نقصا في البيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r1.claim: The inference and its continuation weave reminders of divine favor into the argument.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r1.anchor: وهذا التفريع وما عطف عليه إدماج للامتنان في خلال الاستدلال .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r2.claim: Thumma marks rank rather than ordinary temporal delay: making the human path of action easy is especially astonishing because it follows from intellect, humanity's greatest endowment, and is a major favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r2.anchor: وحرف { ثم } من قوله : { ثم السبيل يسره } للتراخي الرتبي لأن تيسير سبيل العمل الإنساني أعجب في الدلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r3.claim: Al-sabīl means a road and is a metaphor for human deeds and conduct, which are like a path a traveler walks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r3.anchor: و { السبيل } : الطريق ، وهو هنا مستعار لما يفعله الإنسان من أعماله وتصرفاته تشبيها للأعمال بطريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r4.claim: Alternatively, al-sabīl may denote the newborn's passage from the womb, called one of the two passages; this reading links emergence into the world with the following death and burial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مستعارا لمسقط المولود من بطن أمه فقد أطلق على ذلك الممر اسم السبيل في قولهم : ( السبيلان )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r5.claim: On the birth-passage reading, God's creating the human and making him emerge are paired with causing death and burying him, burial being the opposite of emergence onto earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r5.anchor: ف { أماته } مقابل { خلقه } و { أقبره } مقابل { ثم السبيل يسره } لأن الإقبار إدخال في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r6.anchor: والتيسير : التسهيل ، و { السبيل } منصوب بفعل مضمر على طريق الاشتغال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r7.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative under an omitted verb by the construction of الاشتغال, with the pronoun referring back to it; the implied wording is yassara al-sabīla lahu, like 54:17.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r7.anchor: و { السبيل } منصوب بفعل مضمر على طريق الاشتغال ، والضمير عائد إلى { السبيل } . والتقدير : يسر السبيل له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r8.claim: Putting al-sabīl before its verb draws attention to the lesson of the easy path in both metaphorical senses and maintains the verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#21/r8.anchor: وتقديم { السبيل } على فعله للاهتمام بالعبرة بتيسير السبيل بمعنييه المجازيين ، وفيه رعاية للفواصل .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r1.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say God made knowledge of the path of truth and falsehood easy for the human being.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما سهل له العلم بطريق الحق والباطل قاله الحسن ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r2.claim: Al-Farra construes the phrase as meaning that God then made the path easy for him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r2.anchor: قال الفراء والمعنى ثم يسره للسبيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r3.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r3.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil say God made the path of birth easy for the human being as he emerged from his mother’s womb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p31#3/r3.anchor: والثاني يسر له السبيل في خروجه من بطن أمه قاله السدي ومقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7288/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7288/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7288/r4.claim: God made obedience's path easy, showing human action and prior capacity, so even an unbeliever can be enabled to believe.
JISHUMI:v10p7288/r4.anchor: تعالى سهل سبيل الطاعة، فدل أن ذلك فعل العبد، وأن القدرة قبل الفعل؛

MUJAHID:v2p730#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p730#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p730#3/r1.claim: Mujahid understands God making the way easy as parallel to the statement that He guided the person to the way (76:3).
MUJAHID:v2p730#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ثم السبيل يسره ﴾ قال هو مثل قوله ﴿ إنا هديناه السبيل ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r1.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative through an implied verb yassara, meaning He then made the way easy.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r1.anchor: نصب السبيل باضمار يسر أى ثم سهل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r2.claim: One explanation is that God facilitated the way out of the mother's womb.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r2.anchor: له سبيل الخروج من بطن أمه أو بين له

NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r3.claim: Alternatively, God made the way of good and evil clear to him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#18/r3.anchor: أو بين له سبيل الخير والشر

BURSEVI:v10p261/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p261/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p261/r1.claim: On either interpretation, the fāʾ gives detail, because the implied meaning already contains the action it explicates.
BURSEVI:v10p261/r1.anchor: وعلى الوجهين فالفاء للتفصيل فإن التقدير يتضمنه عى المعنيين

BURSEVI:v10p261/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p261/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p261/r2.claim: On the bodily reading, God makes birth possible by opening the previously closed womb and directing the infant to turn head down.
BURSEVI:v10p261/r2.anchor: أي سهل مخرجه من البطن بأن فتح فم الرحم وكان غير مفتوح قبل الولادة وألهمه أن ينتكس

BURSEVI:v10p261/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p261/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p261/r3.claim: On the moral reading, God makes paths of good and evil accessible by granting capacity, explaining benefit and harm, reason, prophets, and revealed books.
BURSEVI:v10p261/r3.anchor: أو يسر له سبيل الخير والشر في الدين ومكنه من السلوك فيهما وذلك بالأقدار والتعريف له بما هو نافع

BURSEVI:v10p261/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p261/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p261/r4.claim: The definite form al-sabīl rather than a possessive phrase signals generality: it applies to humans and jinn in the moral reading, and animals too in the birth reading.
BURSEVI:v10p261/r4.anchor: وتعريف السبيل باللام دون الإضافة بأن يقال سبيله للإشعار بعمومه لأنه عام للأنس والجن

BURSEVI:v10p261/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p261/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v10p261/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says God makes the path easy for the person destined for success, so that they seek right guidance and salvation.
BURSEVI:v10p261/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله يسر على من قدر له التوفيق طلب رشده واتباع نجاته

BURSEVI:v10p261/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p261/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
BURSEVI:v10p261/r6.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir says God makes easy for each person what He created and decreed for them.
BURSEVI:v10p261/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر رحمه الله يسر على كل أحد ما خلقه له وقدره عليه

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r1.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative through an elided yassiruhu, which is then supplied as its explanation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r1.anchor: نصب السبيل بإضمار يسره ، وفسره بيسره

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r2.speaker: القول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r2.claim: One view is that God facilitated the infant's exit from the womb: the child turns from its initial position at birth, and surviving passage through the narrow opening is wondrous.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r2.anchor: المراد تسهيل خروجه من بطن أمه

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r3.claim: Abū Muslim equates this with 90:10: God enables a person to choose good or evil in worldly and religious matters through capacity, instruction, reason, prophets, and revealed books.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المراد من هذه الآية ، هو المراد من قوله : { وهديناه النجدين }

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r4.speaker: القول الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r4.claim: A third view restricts the facilitated path to religion, reasoning that al-sabīl suggests worldly conditions rather than matters attained in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r4.anchor: أن هذا مخصوص بأمر الدين ، لأن لفظ السبيل مشعر بأن المقصود أحوال الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī places the facilitated path in the middle stage of human life and then identifies death, burial, and resurrection as the final stage.
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#4/r5.anchor: وأما المرتبة الثانية : وهي المرتبة الأخيرة ، فهي قوله تعالى : { ثم أماته فأقبره

STUDYQURAN:80:20/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r1.speaker: IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r1.claim: One interpretation is that God made birth easy, so the baby can come forth from the mother's womb.
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r1.anchor: From one perspective, this verse refers to the ease with which a baby comes forth from the mother’s womb (IK, Q)

STUDYQURAN:80:20/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that God made the way easy by providing all people with guidance, as 76:3 says.
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r2.anchor: it refers to God’s providing all people with guidance, as in 76:3: Truly We guided him upon the way, be he grateful or ungrateful (IK).

STUDYQURAN:80:20/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r3.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r3.claim: A further interpretation is that God makes it easy for each thing to perform the function for which it was created.
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r3.anchor: Some interpret it as an indication that God has made it easy for everything to perform the function

STUDYQURAN:80:20/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r4.claim: The source cites a famous hadith saying that each person’s created function has been made easy for them.
STUDYQURAN:80:20/r4.anchor: in a famous ḥadīth, “Work, for that for which each person was created has been made easy for him”

TAB-FULL:v24p113/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r1.claim: Mujāhid understands the path as the paths of misery and happiness, linking it to 76:3.
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: سبيل الشقاء والسعادة

TAB-FULL:v24p113/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan, as reported by Qatāda, glosses the path as the path of good.
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r2.anchor: قال: قال الحسن، في قوله: {ثم السبيل يسره}

TAB-FULL:v24p113/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says God guided the person to Islam, made it easy, and taught it to him.
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ثم السبيل يسره}

TAB-FULL:v24p113/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers “the way” as the facilitated passage out of the mother's womb, because the surrounding verses describe creation, bodily development, and changing states.
TAB-FULL:v24p113/r4.anchor: وأولى التأويلين في ذلك عندي بالصواب قول من قال: ثم الطريق

SULAMI:v2p373#7/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#7/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p373#7/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says the path is made easy for the one destined for success to seek right guidance and follow the way of salvation.
SULAMI:v2p373#7/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : يسر على من قدر له التوفيق طلب رشده واتباع نجاته

SULAMI:v2p373#7/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p373#7/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p373#7/r2.claim: Abū Bakr b. Ṭāhir says God makes easy for each person whatever He creates and decrees for that person.
SULAMI:v2p373#7/r2.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : يسر على كل أحد ما يخلقه له وقدر عليه

TABRISI:80:20/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:80:20/r4.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative after an implicit verb explained by yassarah: then He made the way easy for the human; the prepositional phrase is omitted.
TABRISI:80:20/r4.anchor: انتصب السبيل بفعل مضمر يفسره هذا الظاهر تقديره ثم يسر السبيل يسره له أي للإنسان ثم حذف الجار والمجرور

TABRISI:80:20#2/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20#2/r24.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:80:20#2/r24.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say God made the birth route from the mother's womb easy: He turned the baby's orientation at delivery to ease its exit.
TABRISI:80:20#2/r24.anchor: أي ثم يسر سبيل الخروج من بطن أمه حتى خرج منه عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:80:20#2/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:80:20#2/r25.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:80:20#2/r25.claim: Another view takes the way as the path of religion: God showed good and evil and enabled the human to do good and avoid evil.
TABRISI:80:20#2/r25.anchor: وقيل: ثم السبيل أي سبيل الدين يسره وطريق الخير والشر بين له وخيره ومكنه من فعل الخير واجتناب الشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r1.speaker: الحسن، ومجاهد، وعطاء، والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r1.claim: They take the path as the way of good and evil, which God made known to humanity, as in 76:3.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r1.anchor: قال الحسن (¬6)، ومجاهد (¬7)، وعطاء (¬8) (¬9)، # والكلبي (¬1) (¬2): بين له سبيل الخير، والشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r2.speaker: السدي، ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r2.claim: They interpret it as God bringing the child out of the womb and guiding him to emerge from his mother's body.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p223/r2.anchor: قال السدي (¬3)، ومقاتل (¬4): أي أخرجه من الرحم، وهداه للخروج من بطن أمه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r1.claim: God made the path of birth out of the mother's womb easy for the human.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:80:20-28/r1.anchor: ثم السبيل يسره } أي: طريق خروجه من بطن أمه.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r1.claim: Late readers’ mistakes do not discredit the Qurʾan; later non-Arab generations lacked native linguistic instinct and mishandled many readings.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r1.anchor: وكذلك لحن اللاحنين من القراء المتأخرين، لا يجعل حجة على الكتاب. وقد كان الناس قديما يقرؤون بلغاتهم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r2.claim: The unnamed reader is inconsistent, applying features to some words but not analogous ones, contradicting his own rules, and choosing readings with only strained justifications.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r2.anchor: لم أر فيمن تتبعت وجوه قراءته أكثر تخليطا، ولا أشد اضطرابا منه، لأنه يستعمل في الحرف ما يدعه في نظيره

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r3.claim: He departs from Arab and Hijazi usage through excessive lengthening, hamza, imāla, and assimilation, imposing difficult recitation and narrowing what God made easy.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r3.anchor: هذا إلى نبذه في قراءته مذاهب العرب وأهل الحجاز، فإفراطه في المد والهمزة والإشباع، وإفحاشه في الإضجاع والإدغام، وحمله المتعلمين على المركب الصعب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r4.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna held that a worshipper who recited in this reader’s ḥarf, or prayed behind his recitation, had to repeat the prayer.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r4.anchor: وكان ابن عيينة يرى لمن قرأ في صلاته بحرفه، أو ائتم بقراءته: أن يعيد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r5.speaker: بشر بن الحارث وأحمد بن حنبل
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r5.claim: Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and many other distinguished Muslims agreed with Ibn ʿUyayna’s ruling to repeat the prayer.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r5.anchor: ووافقه على ذلك كثير من خيار المسلمين منهم بشر بن الحارث وأحمد بن حنبل.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r6.claim: Common people prized this recitation because its difficulty and long training seemed impressive, and the reader’s strained facial expression and sweat looked like expertise.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r6.anchor: وقد شغف بقراءته عوام الناس وسوقهم، وليس ذلك إلا لما يرونه من مشقتها وصعوبتها، وطول اختلاف المتعلم إلى المقرئ فيها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r7.claim: The Prophet, early Muslims, Successors, and learned reciters read smoothly and easily; this is the style the author chooses for regular recitation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r7.anchor: وليس هكذا كانت قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، ولا خيار السلف ولا التابعين، ولا القراء العالمين، بل كانت قراءتهم سهلة رسلة. وهكذا نختار

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r8.claim: For a young beginner he favors careful training that loosens the tongue and removes speech impediments, but without excessive lengthening, hamza, or assimilation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p42/r8.anchor: فنختار له أن يؤخذ بالتحقيق عليه، من غير إفحاش في مد أو همز أو إدغام، لأن في ذلك تذليلا للسان، وإطلاقا من الحبسة، وحلا للعقدة.

RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p55#3/r4.claim: The discussion proceeds from human proportioning to God's facilitation of the path.

TAB-FULL:v24p111/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r3.claim: He says God made the path easy for the human, while reporting disagreement about which path is meant.
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r3.anchor: {ثم السبيل يسره} [عبس: 20] يقول: ثم يسره للسبيل، يعني للطريق واختلف أهل التأويل في السبيل

TAB-FULL:v24p111/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the facilitated path as the child's passage out of its mother's womb.
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {ثم السبيل يسره} [عبس: 20] يعني بذلك: خروجه من بطن أمه يسره له

TAB-FULL:v24p111/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r5.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r5.claim: Abu Salih calls it the path of the womb.
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r5.anchor: عن سفيان، عن إسماعيل، عن أبي صالح، {ثم السبيل يسره} [عبس: 20] قال: سبيل الرحم

TAB-FULL:v24p111/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r6.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the path as the child's exit from its mother's womb.
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r6.anchor: عن السدي، {ثم السبيل يسره} [عبس: 20] قال: خروجه من بطن أمه

TAB-FULL:v24p111/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r7.claim: Qatada also identifies the path as the child's exit from its mother's womb.
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r7.anchor: عن قتادة {ثم السبيل يسره} [عبس: 20] قال: أخرجه من بطن

TAB-FULL:v24p111/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r8.claim: Mujahid says the path is the route of right and wrong made clear and accessible, comparing it to 76:3.
TAB-FULL:v24p111/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ثم السبيل يسره} [عبس: 20] قال: هو كقوله: {إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا} [الإنسان: 3]

TABATABAI:80:19-20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r3.claim: In context, the unqualified path is the way to obey God and attain good and happiness; this reading answers the claim that divine creation and decree make human acts compulsory.
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r3.anchor: ظاهر السياق المقصود به نفي العذر من الإنسان في كفره واستكباره أن المراد بالسبيل

TABATABAI:80:19-20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r4.claim: God's creation and decree do not negate choice: divine will concerns humans acting by their own will, so their acts are both decreed and chosen, and they remain accountable.
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r4.anchor: ومحصله أن الخلق والتقدير لا ينافيان كون الانسان مختارا فيما أمر به من الإيمان والطاعة

TABATABAI:80:19-20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r5.claim: One alternative takes the path to mean the facilitated delivery of the human from his mother's womb.
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد بتيسير السبيل تسهيل خروج الانسان من بطن أمه والمعنى ثم سهل للانسان الخروج

TABATABAI:80:19-20/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r6.claim: Another alternative understands the path as guidance to religion and clarification of the ways of good and evil.
TABATABAI:80:19-20/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد الهداية إلى الدين وتبين طريق الخير والشر

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r4.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r4.claim: Exegetes understand “then He made the way easy” either as facilitating birth from the womb or as enabling a choice between good and evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r4.anchor: müfessirler “Ana rahminden çıkmayı kolaylaştırdı” veya “Hayır yahut şer yolunu seçme imkânı verdi” şeklinde yorumlamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r5.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r5.claim: Tabari prefers the interpretation that God facilitated the human’s emergence from the womb, based on the verse’s context.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r5.anchor: Taberî âyetin bağlamını dikkate alarak birinci yorumu tercih etmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r6.claim: The author prefers the second sense: humans were granted the capacity to choose between good and evil, faith and disbelief, and right and wrong, a gift worthy of remembrance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r6.anchor: insanın iyilik-kötülük, iman-inkâr, doğru-yanlış şeklindeki alternatifler arasında seçim yapma gücüne sahip varlık olarak yaratılması daha çok hatırlatılmaya değer bir lütuftur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r7.claim: This capacity distinguishes humans from all other created beings and gives them a measure of freedom alongside their responsibility to obey God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:80:17/r7.anchor: Bu özelliğiyle insan dünyadaki diğer bütün yaratılmışlardan üstün ve seçkin kılınmıştır

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r25.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r25.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r25.claim: God made the path easy in both good and evil and inspired the human being in how to act.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r25.anchor: يسر عليه السبيل في الخير والشر ، وألهمه كيف التصرف

QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r26.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r26.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r26.claim: An alternative reading is that God made birth easy, so the child emerges from the womb head first and upside down.
QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r26.anchor: ويقال : يسر عليه الخروج من بطن أمه يخرج أولا رأسه منكوسا

AKHFASH:v2p567/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p567/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p567/r5.claim: He explains the wording with the equivalent expression hadāhu al-ṭarīq, illustrating the relation between the path and the person guided.

FARRA:v3p237/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p237/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p237/r2.claim: The phrase means He made the path easy for him; هديناه السبيل means He showed him the paths of good and evil.
FARRA:v3p237/r2.anchor: ثم يسره للسبيل، ومثله: «إنا هديناه السبيل

NAHHAS:v5p151/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p151/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
NAHHAS:v5p151/r5.claim: The best explanation reported from Ibn al-Zubayr is that God made the birth passage easy for the child until it emerged from the womb.
NAHHAS:v5p151/r5.anchor: وأولى ما قيل في معنى 20 قول عبد الله بن الزبير رحمه الله أنه يسره أي سهل عليه حتى خرج من الرحم

NAHHAS:v5p151/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p151/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p151/r6.claim: The construction has an omitted ل in للسبيل; يسر takes two objects, one introduced by a preposition.
NAHHAS:v5p151/r6.anchor: والتقدير في العربية ثم للسبيل وحذف اللام لأنه مما يتعدى إلى مفعولين أحدهما بحرف

ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r6.claim: God guided the human along the way, whether grateful or ungrateful.
ZAJJAJ:v5p284/r6.anchor: أي هداه السبيل (إما شاكرا وإما كفورا)

ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.claim: Although verses 18–22 use the past tense, Asad says they describe a recurring phenomenon.
ASAD-NOTES:80:17#n6/r2.anchor: Verses 18-22, although formulated in the past tense, obviously describe a recurrent phenomenon.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r13.claim: God made easy the way out of the mother's womb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r13.anchor: أي طريق خروجه من بطن أمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r14.speaker: السدي ومقاتل والحسن ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r14.claim: Al-Suddi, Muqatil, al-Hasan, and Mujahid say God made clear the paths of truth and falsehood, citing 76:3 and 90:10.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r14.anchor: قال السدي ومقاتل، والحسن ومجاهد: يعني طريق الحق والباطل، سهل له العلم به،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r15.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r15.claim: Another view says God eases for each person what He created and decreed for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p337/r15.anchor: وقيل: يسر على كل أحد ما خلقه له وقدره عليه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r7.claim: God eased the person's exit from his mother's womb by opening the womb and inspiring him to turn headfirst, or made the path of good and evil easy for him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r7.anchor: ثم سهل مخرجه من بطن أمه بأن فتح فوهة الرحم وألهمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r8.claim: The accusative is governed by a verb explained by the following verb, intensifying the sense of ease.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r8.anchor: ونصب السبيل بفعل يفسره الظاهر للمبالغة في التيسير

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r9.claim: Using the definite article rather than a possessive construction signals a path common to all.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r9.anchor: وتعريفه باللام دون الإضافة للإشعار بأنه سبيل عام

BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r10.claim: On the moral-path reading, the verse hints that worldly life is a road whose destination lies elsewhere.
BAYDAWI-FULL:80:17-20/r10.anchor: وفيه على المعنى الأخير إيماء بأن الدنيا طريق والمقصد غيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r8.claim: The way is the human’s route out of the womb and, more broadly, the route to Paradise or Hell; God eases birth by opening the womb and turning the child into position.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r8.anchor: وهو مخرجه من بطن أمه وطريقه إلى الجنة أو النار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r9.claim: God also makes the good and evil paths accessible and gives reason to guide a person toward whichever path is eased for him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r9.anchor: سبيل الخير والشر , وجعل له عقلا يقوده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r10.claim: This hints that worldly life is only a passage and the true destination is the next life, which the present world indicates.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p328/r10.anchor: والمقصد غيرها وهو الأخرى التي تدل عليها الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says the path made easy is the child’s easy exit from the mother’s womb.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r13.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ثم السبيل يسره} يعني بذلك خروجه من بطن أمه

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r14.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r14.claim: Ikrima glosses the easy path as the child’s exit from the womb.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r14.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن عكرمة {ثم السبيل يسره} قال: خروجه من الرحم

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r15.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r15.claim: Qatada says the easy path is the child’s exit from the mother’s womb.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r15.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وعبد بن حميد عن قتادة {ثم السبيل يسره} قال: خروجه من بطن أمه

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r16.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak gives the same interpretation: exit from the womb.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r16.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الضحاك مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r17.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r17.claim: Abu Salih also glosses the path as the child’s exit from the womb.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r17.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن أبي صالح {ثم السبيل يسره} قال: خروجه من الرحم

DURR-FULL:v8p418/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r18.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r18.claim: Mujahid links the easy path to 76:3, taking it as the path of misery and felicity, with a person either grateful or ungrateful.
DURR-FULL:v8p418/r18.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن مجاهد في قوله: {ثم السبيل يسره} قال: هو كقوله: (إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكر وإما كفورا)

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r4.claim: Thumma signals rank, not mere time: facilitating the human path of action is more wondrous as an effect of intellect and a greater favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r4.anchor: وحرف { ثم } من قوله : { ثم السبيل يسره } للتراخي الرتبي لأن تيسير سبيل العمل الإنساني أعجب في الدلالة على بديع صنع الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r5.claim: The ‘path’ can metaphorically mean a person’s actions and conduct, compared to a road a traveler walks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r5.anchor: و { السبيل } : الطريق ، وهو هنا مستعار لما يفعله الإنسان من أعماله وتصرفاته تشبيها للأعمال بطريق يمشي فيه الماشي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r6.claim: Alternatively, al-sabīl may mean the birth passage, called al-sabīlān; this pairs delivery with death and burial as opposed movements into and out of the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مستعارا لمسقط المولود من بطن أمه فقد أطلق على ذلك الممر اسم السبيل في قولهم : ( السبيلان )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r7.claim: Taysīr means making easy; the implied verb is ‘He made the path easy for him,’ comparable to making the Qur’an easy for remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r7.anchor: والتيسير : التسهيل ، و { السبيل } منصوب بفعل مضمر على طريق الاشتغال ، والضمير عائد إلى { السبيل } . والتقدير : يسر السبيل له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r8.claim: The path is advanced before its verb to highlight the lesson in its facilitation and preserve verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p123/r8.anchor: وتقديم { السبيل } على فعله للاهتمام بالعبرة بتيسير السبيل بمعنييه المجازيين ، وفيه رعاية للفواصل .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi take the way as the route out of the womb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وقتادة وأبو صالح والسدي: هي سبيل الخروج من بطن المرأة ورحمها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan takes it as sound reflection leading to faith, made easy by reason.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن ما معناه: إن السبيل هي سبيل النظر القويم المؤدي إلى الإيمان،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r9.claim: Mujahid takes the way as guidance or misguidance and relates it to 76:3 and 90:10.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p438#2/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أراد السبيل عامة اسم الجنس في هدى وضلال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, along with Ikrima, al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, Qatada, and al-Suddi, interprets the facilitated path as the child's exit from its mother's womb; Ibn Jarir chose this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r7.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: ثم يسر عليه خروجه من بطن أمه. وكذا قال عكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، وقتادة، والسدي، واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r8.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd understand the path as guidance made clear and action made easy, like 76:3; Ibn Kathir says this is the stronger view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p322#3/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هذه كقوله: {إنا هديناه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا} [الإنسان: 3]

JISHUMI:v10p7285/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7285/r4.claim: Al-sabīl is in the accusative as the object of yassara.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r7.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative by an elided yassara, which the following yassara explains.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r7.anchor: نصب السبيل بإضمار ( يسر ) وفسره بيسر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r8.claim: The path may be the passage out of the mother’s womb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r8.anchor: ثم سهل سبيله وهو مخرجه من بطن أمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r9.claim: Alternatively, it is the path of good or evil a person chooses, made accessible through ability and empowerment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r9.anchor: أو السبيل الذي يختار سلوكه من طريقي الخير والشر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the path as God making clear the way of good and the way of evil.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p703#2/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : بين له سبيل الخير والشر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r8.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r8.claim: The path made easy is the route of birth from the mother’s womb.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r8.anchor: خروجه من بطن أمه , قاله عكرمة والضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r9.claim: The path can mean the path of happiness or misery.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r10.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r10.claim: The path can mean the path of guidance or misguidance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p205/r11.claim: A further possibility is that God makes easy the paths of a person’s benefits and harms.

MUQATIL:80:18-23/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:80:18-23/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:80:18-23/r3.claim: God eases the way out of the mother’s womb; the human should reflect, affirm God’s oneness, and thank Him for His blessings and good creation.
MUQATIL:80:18-23/r3.anchor: يعني هون طريقه في الخروج من بطن أمه يقول يسره للخروج أفلا يعتبر فيوحد الله في حسن خلقه فيشكر الله في نعمه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Ata, along with Qatada, al-Suddi, and Muqatil, says God made the path out of the mother's womb easy.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل: يسره للخروج من بطن أمه

QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r3.claim: Mujahid says God made the paths of good and evil clear, supported by the guidance and two paths mentioned elsewhere; Hasan, Ata, and Ibn Abbas through Abu Salih also give this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r3.anchor: مجاهد: يسره لطريق الخير والشر أي بين له ذلك. دليله: إنا هديناه السبيل

QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r4.claim: Mujahid also glosses the path as the path of wretchedness and felicity.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r4.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا قال: سبيل الشقاء والسعادة

QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the path as Islam.

QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r6.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says God makes easy for each person what He created and decreed for that person, supported by the Prophet's saying that everyone is facilitated toward what he was created for.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r6.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر: يسر على كل أحد ما خلقه له، وقدره عليه دليله قوله عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r7.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r7.claim: The Prophet says: act, for each person is facilitated toward what he was created for.
QURTUBI-FULL:80:19-20/r7.anchor: وقدره عليه دليله قوله عليه السلام:
